content:
The test image shows corn plants with severe lodging — multiple stalks have collapsed or are leaning, leaves are dead/dried, with a field-wide distribution. This points to a stalk rot disease. Key candidates: Charcoal stalk rot, Anthracnose stalk rot, Diplodia stalk rot, Gibberella/Fusarium stalk rot.

Let me view reference images for the top candidates in parallel.
Anthracnose stalk rot reference shows field-level lodging similar to test image. Diplodia also shows lodging. Let me view more candidates to distinguish.
Physoderma stalk rot shows widespread field lodging (top-left panel) very similar to the test image. Let me also check Anthracnose leaf spot and Northern corn leaf blight for comparison.
Let me view a few more critical reference images to confirm between my top candidates.

Now I have enough information. Let me consolidate my analysis:

**Test image key observations:**
- Full-sized corn plants (not stunted) that have completely collapsed/lodged
- All leaves are dead, dry, tan/brown — late-season complete plant death
- Multiple plants lodged uniformly across the same area
- Stalks appear light tan/brown colored (not obviously shiny black)
- Plants appear to have broken near lower nodes

**Ruling out candidates:**
- Downy mildew, Corn Stunt Spiroplasma, Crazy top, MDMV — wrong symptoms (green/virus/foliar)
- Bacterial stalk rot — plants usually scattered, not clustered; foul odor; vascular strands intact
- Anthracnose stalk rot — shiny **black** rind visible on stalk; test stalks are light tan
- Physoderma stalk rot — black nodes at first/second internode; reference shows breaking at specific node
- Charcoal stalk rot — internal gray charcoal appearance; external stalk can look similar but less widespread lodging pattern

**Best match — Diplodia stalk rot:**
- Classic cause of widespread pre-harvest lodging with completely dead, dried plants
- Reference shows similar field view of many lodged/fallen plants with tan/brown dried leaves
- "Die prematurely" matches total plant death seen in test image
- Light tan/brown stalk appearance (not shiny black like Anthracnose)
- Most common and severe cause of mass stalk failure and lodging in corn

```json
{"prediction": "Diplodia_stalk_rot", "confidence": 0.48, "reasoning": "The test image shows full-sized corn plants with widespread, uniform late-season lodging and complete plant death (all leaves dry/tan). Stalks are light tan/brown — not shiny black (ruling out Anthracnose) and no obvious black nodes (ruling out Physoderma). Diplodia stalk rot is the most common cause of pre-harvest mass stalk failure and lodging with this pattern of completely dead, dried plants collapsing across multiple rows. Confidence is moderate because stalk internal details (pycnidia, shredded pith) are not visible in the field-level photo."}
```
